final_answer:
MEMORANDUM (privileged) | To: M. Calloway | From: J. Reeves | Re: Silverpeak/Ridgeway redline, Cascade Growth Fund III

1. BOTTOM LINE
- Do not sign June 6. Four deal-stoppers: (i) Buyer ERISA rep deleted (Redline 5.7); (ii) interim Voting Direction (5.8); (iii) uncapped indemnity (6.3(a)); (iv) 3-year non-compete (7.9). (i) and (ii) can sink GP consent; (iii) and (iv) need David Koehler's written approval to concede (Playbook "PB" 1, 11; oral insufficient), which we recommend withholding. Escalate tonight.
- The redline is not a true redline of our draft: header says "Original Dated May 20" (ours went May 22); it is re-papered (new numbering, exhibits, definitions) with many untracked changes (Part 4). XML shows 36 insertions and 21 deletions (about 28 discrete edits; Margaret counted ~47). Demand a true comparison against May 22.
- Seller-side effect: closing cash $31,960,800 falls to $28,409,600; holdback Buyer-held for 270 days; price re-openable downward by a Buyer-chosen valuer; indemnity uncapped; capital-call indemnity up to $1,325,000.
- Timing: July 1 Effective Date is doubtful. Notice due within 5 Business Days of signing (6/13); LPA 9.3(a) gives the GP 30 days from the first Business Day after a Complete Transfer Package (about 7/16), tolled by information requests (9.3(c)); ROFR 15 Business Days, concurrent (11.2(b)); silence is deemed denial with a 90-day resubmission bar (9.3(b)). Consent after 6/30 means an October 1 Effective Date, after the 9/15 Outside Closing Date. Pre-clear terms with the GP via Hargrove & Sitwell and ask for early consent and ROFR waiver. Our draft's Interim Period ends at Closing though Seller stays LP of record until the Effective Date; extend it.

2. PRIORITY
A Critical: ERISA; Voting Direction; cap removal; non-compete; holdback; true-up; 6.5 indemnity; cooperation.
B Significant: first-dollar basket; survival; NY law/courts/jury waiver; Affiliate assignment; untracked changes.
C Minor: Business Day; email notice; Attn line; Schedule A; severability.

3. MATERIAL DEVIATIONS (Clean = May 22 draft; PB = Playbook)

A1 ERISA rep deleted. Clean 3.2(h) tied to LPA 9.5. PB 8.1(c): "non-negotiable"; transaction-stopping; MP approval (11(d)). LPA 9.2(a) requires ERISA reps before any Transfer; 9.5(c) makes failure to deliver requested ERISA reps "grounds for the denial of consent"; 9.5(a)(iv) bars plan-asset status, tested on Benefit Plan Investor holdings before and after; Eligible Transferee prong (c) excludes Benefit Plan Investors absent GP determination; Exhibit D joinder requires ERISA status reps. Without it the GP cannot apply the 29 C.F.R. 2510.3-101 test. Recommend REJECT; restore Clean text; ask for Ridgeway's investor look-through (why refuse unless it has plan investors?).

A2 Voting Direction (new 5.8). Seller votes only as Buyer directs; noncompliance is "material breach" (termination 9.1(f), closing condition 8.1(d), uncapped indemnity). PB 5.2: reject, escalate. LPA "Transfer" includes "any transfer of voting or economic rights ... whether or not ... a change in record ownership"; 9.1 voids unconsented Transfers; 9.2(c) gives no rights pre-admission. The clause is itself an unconsented Transfer, visible to the GP in the Transfer Notice. Recommend REJECT; fallback: notice and good-faith consultation only, Seller keeps discretion, no proxy.

A3 Cap deleted (6.3(a); definition struck). Clean 6.4(b): $5,326,800 (15%). PB 4.1: firm; uncapped "under no circumstances"; MP approval (11(b)). Exposure unlimited, at least the $35,512,000 price. Recommend REJECT; restore. Own-draft issue: Clean 6.4(c) exempts willful misconduct and Fundamental Representations from cap and basket, beyond PB 4.1 (fraud only); confirm Koehler approved, else conform or cap at Purchase Price (MP approval).

A4 Holdback. 20% ($7,102,400) versus 10% ($3,551,200): +$3,551,200 (100% over PB); 270 versus 120 days (+150); closing cash -11.1%; "retained by Buyer" (untracked; Clean 2.3(b) used escrow, earnings to Seller; PB 2.3 bars Buyer-held "under no circumstances"). 20% also exceeds the 15% cap. A 9/15 closing releases June 12, 2026. At an assumed 8% cost of capital (illustrative), carry is about $420,000 versus about $93,000. MP approval (11(a)). Recommend REJECT; restore 10%/120 days/independent escrow. No fallback without Koehler.

A5 True-up (new 2.5). Buyer-selected valuer, Buyer-"reasonable" methodology, downward only, measured at the Effective Date against March 31 NAV, final absent manifest error, Seller pays shortfall in 10 Business Days. PB 2.1-2.2(a)-(c): prohibited. Clean 2.2: fixed price. Flaws: reduces dollar-for-dollar though price is 92% of NAV; double counts distributions already deducted under 2.4(b); Effective Date may follow the 90-day window. 5% NAV fall = $1,930,000; 10% = $3,860,000, uncapped. LPA 11.2(d): price reduction or material term change after ROFR waiver requires new Transfer Notice; whether a disclosed contingent true-up does is arguable. Recommend REJECT; only PB-compliant alternative is an audited-financials true-up within 30 days of next audit, which we would not volunteer.

A6 New 6.5 capital-call indemnity. Seller covers calls in 12 months above $2,500,000, "regardless" of source or any commitment increase; outside basket; 18-month survival. Clean 2.1/7.2/7.6 put post-Effective Date calls on Buyer, who assumed $3,825,000. PB 4.3(a),(c): resist. Exposure up to $1,325,000 on existing commitment (34.6% of unfunded), more if commitments increase (LPA excerpts silent). LPA 9.4(a) limits Seller to a 60-day tail and the Unfunded Commitment; 9.4(c) bars side arrangements extending Seller's obligations to the Partnership or GP. 6.5 runs to Buyer so is no literal breach, but the GP may read a Seller backstop as undercutting 9.2(b)(ii) full assumption. Recommend REJECT; offer restoration of Clean 7.5 (Buyer posts 9.4(b) letter of credit or cash escrow, ending Seller's tail) with Buyer indemnity.

A7 Non-compete (new 7.9). 3 years; Seller and Affiliates barred from acquiring/holding any fund of the GP or any growth fund over $500,000,000 (defined twice); only pre-signing holdings grandfathered; injunction and irreparable-harm admission. PB 7: none "of any kind"; MP escalation (11(c)); hits Silverpeak's growth strategy and successor GP funds. Recommend REJECT; offer only confirmation that no option over the Interest exists.

A8 Cooperation (7.8). 18 months versus 60 days; $25,000 cap deleted; staff (tax, accounting) 40 hours/quarter (240 hours); "investor communications". PB 6: 60 days, $25,000, no hourly commitments. Recommend counter: Clean 7.4 terms; accept (a), (c), (d); reject (b); Buyer reimburses excess within 15 business days.

B1 Basket. First-dollar versus deductible $355,120 (1%); on $500,000 of losses Seller pays $500,000 not $144,880 (+$355,120). PB 4.2: must not concede. Basket also Seller-only, covering 6.1(a) only. Recommend REJECT. Drafting: Clean and PB call a deductible a "tipping basket", opposite to market usage; say "deductible".

B2 Survival. General 36 months (PB max 12); Fundamental "statute of limitations plus 60 days" (PB 3.2: max 24 months; SOL language barred); covenants "indefinitely". Fundamental reps now include No Broker. SOL longer under NY law (six years CPLR 213(2); Delaware three years, 10 Del. C. 8106; from memory, unverified). Recommend REJECT; 12/24 months, mutual. Any concession needs MP approval.

B3 NY law; courts; jury waiver deleted. PB 9.1-9.2: Delaware, JAMS, no litigation without mutual jury waiver; MP approval (11(e),(f)). LPA 15.1 is Delaware, so NY creates split regimes and loses confidentiality of NAV data; NY generally enforces NY choice for large deals (GOL 5-1401, from memory). Recommend REJECT all; if Koehler authorizes, trade forum only (Delaware law and mutual jury waiver kept).

B4 Affiliate assignment (10.4). Drops Clean conditions (assignee Eligible Transferee; Seller-satisfactory assumption). Changing the Transferee requires new notice, ROFR and consent (LPA 11.2(d), 9.1, 9.2(a)). Counter: restore conditions; only to Affiliate disclosed in the Transfer Notice, ERISA-clean; no delay of consent; Buyer remains liable.

C Minor: Business Day "banks open in New York" (accept; match LPA definition, not excerpted, since 9.3/11.2 count Business Days); email notice with Schedule A placeholders (accept; keep acknowledgment); Attn Vasquez; Schedule A; severability (accept; drop good-faith replacement proviso if it could revive a deleted covenant). Unchanged and confirmed: price $35,512,000 (92% of $38,600,000), Outside Closing Date, ROFR/consent acknowledgments, Seller bears Transfer Fee (up to $50,000, LPA 9.6).

4. UNTRACKED DIFFERENCES FROM OUR DRAFT (restore or justify)
- Price: Clean no-true-up sentence gone; Purchase Price "subject to 2.5"; 2.4(c) nets interim calls/distributions against holdback, settled 5 Business Days after release (Clean: at Closing; PB 5.1); administrator verification deleted.
- 6.1(c) pre-Effective Date Fund/Interest taxes and 6.1(d) third-party claims added to Seller indemnity, outside basket; unilateral special indemnities (PB 4.3), partnership taxes beyond Seller control. Strike.
- Clean protections dropped: mutual cap and basket, mitigation, claim procedures, Buyer tail-security covenant (7.5), tax cooperation/743(b)/754 (7.3), post-Effective Date mechanics (7.6), no-assignment (7.7), confidentiality survival, mutual specific performance, Buyer no-reliance on projections, Buyer financial capacity incl. tail security, regulatory covenant (Clean 5.6: PTP, Securities Act, plan assets, LPA 9.5), Exhibit B Transfer Notice form.
- Buyer assumption narrowed to obligations "arising from and after the Effective Date" (Clean 2.1: all); LPA 9.2(b)(ii)/Exhibit D require assumption of all.
- Seller reps widened: flat capital-account rep (Clean knowledge-qualified), GP LPA-amendment rep (PB 3.1 bars GP reps), qualifiers dropped, "Knowledge" inquiry, new 4.8 Seller PTP/tax rep (PB 8.1(e) puts PTP on Buyer; consider Code 1446(f) withholding), No Broker made fundamental.
- MAE (8.1(g)) runs from Reference Date and covers Fund portfolio "prospects": a Buyer walk right on market moves; restore Clean 4.2(c).
- 3.2(b) has Seller delivering the Joinder (LPA 9.2(b): Buyer); HSR reference (a $35.5M deal is below the size-of-transaction threshold; verify figure).
- Errors in OUR draft: LPA dated October 15, 2017 (excerpts: January 15, 2017, amended through Amendment No. 3, March 1, 2023); counsel email domain tgllaw.com versus thornburygallatin.com; 410 versus PB 400 Park Avenue; Eligible Transferee definition omits LPA prongs (c),(d); no PB 8.1(d)-(e) Buyer reps.
- Data red flag: LPA Schedule A note equates $45,000,000 with a 7.8% interest in $1,150,000,000 of commitments, but that is 3.91% (7.8% is about $89.7M). Reconcile with Arrowpoint before Seller's capital-account rep and notice. Other arithmetic verified.

5. GP CONSENT AND SECTION 9.5 RISK
- Consent is in the GP's "sole and absolute discretion" (9.1); no reasons; deemed denial on silence; the Transfer Notice must state terms and price.
- Highest risk: ERISA deletion; Voting Direction; 6.5 backstop; true-up; Affiliate assignment; Seller-delivered joinder error.
- 9.5 regimes: ERISA (above); PTP (Code 7704): GP may require opinion (9.1(a)(ii), 9.5(c)) at Seller's cost; a block transfer over 2% should fit the safe harbor (Treas. Reg. 1.7704-1(e), from memory, verify) but needs Buyer facts; Securities Act: private resale, investment-intent rep kept (5.3), accredited/QP certifications must precede notice; Investment Company Act via QP status. 9.5(d) consultation costs fall on Seller.
- Complete Transfer Package needs Buyer reps, executed Joinder, any opinion, fee.

6. STRATEGY AND NEXT STEPS
1. Tonight: email Margaret; tell Koehler no signing June 6; PB concessions need his written approval.
2. One response to Ridgeway: reject A1-A7, B1 on LPA/GP-consent grounds; accept C items; demand true comparison.
3. Concessions within PB: email notice, Business Day, cooperation (c),(d), conditioned Affiliate assignment, severability; offer mutual Buyer fundamental reps. Answer David's point: Buyer's assumption of $3,825,000 is already priced at 92%.
4. Hold on cap, deductible, escrow, ERISA, voting, non-compete.
5. Parallel: Hargrove & Sitwell (Feldstein) for full LPA (Business Day, Exhibit D, commitment-increase terms), prescribed notice form, informal GP read; Arrowpoint statements; Ridgeway ERISA/accredited/QP diligence now.
6. Unverified: external-law cites (CPLR, 10 Del. C. 8106, GOL, Treas. Reg., HSR) were unreachable and rest on memory.
